- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:69-104 (also 72, 75, 96-104, 975-985, 981-985, 990-1002, 1004-1015, 1026-1028) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `gh pr list --limit 100` (`DISCOVERY_PR_LIST_LIMIT`) truncates open PRs before the discovery-prefix filter, so older discovery PRs are never seen by either cleanup pass.
  WHY: The stale-manifest conflict persists silently with no truncation signal. Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet, luna, glm) vs MAJOR (gemini, minimax). The highest is recorded here as MAJOR.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:1103-1145 (also scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:659-664, 855-868, 882-968; scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:154, 218, 1134-1146) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `bot_only` human-commit guard is a snapshot from `gh pr list`, and `gh pr close` runs later without re-checking, so a PR that gained a human commit in between can still be closed.
  WHY: This breaks the documented guarantee that a PR with any non-`codex-bot` commit is never closed, and the window is longest in the post-open pass. Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet) vs MAJOR (gemini, minimax, luna, glm).
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:63-116 (`DISCOVERY_COMMIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `_is_bot_only_discovery_pr`, lines 931-946) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The bot-only guard accepts only `codex-bot`, but Claude-engine pipeline writers commit as `claude-bot` (`scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:340`, `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:323`, `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:3437`).
  WHY: Discovery PRs with a `claude-bot` commit are treated as `bot_only=False` and kept as `kept_human_commits`, so the stale-PR conflict persists on Claude-engine consumers. The behavior is fail-safe.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:66-178 (`SEED_PR_TITLE_PREFIX`, matched at line 1083; title built at scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:787-792) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `SEED_PR_TITLE_PREFIX` is a hard-coded copy of the title built in `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py`, and no test pins the coupling.
  WHY: If the runner's title wording changes, `reason=manifest_already_committed` silently stops firing and stale seed PRs accumulate while the tests still pass.
- scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:891-896 (also scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:1134-1146) | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `DiscoveryRunContext` dataclass defaults `close_superseded` to True, so any caller that builds a context directly inherits the auto-close behavior unless it opts out.
  WHY: The gate is documented, but the default is easy to miss. Existing tests opt out explicitly via `close_superseded=False` (tests/test_validation_refresh_runner.py:654).

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:`DISCOVERY_PR_LIST_LIMIT = 100` (line 69) and `--limit` in `list_open_discovery_prs` | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The 100-PR cap is applied before the discovery-prefix filter, so an old discovery PR can be pushed out of the listing and missed by both cleanup passes.
  WHY: Nothing logs when the payload hits the limit, so the miss is invisible. The reviewer did not verify the pass-1 claim about the GitHub node limit and does not report it.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:`bot_only` in `list_open_discovery_prs`; `close_superseded_discovery_prs` | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The human-commit guard uses the `gh pr list` snapshot, and `gh pr close` runs later with no re-check.
  WHY: A person who pushes in the window still has the PR closed. The window is longer in the post-open pass, and the damage is bounded because the branch is kept and the PR can be reopened.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:`DISCOVERY_COMMIT_AUTHOR_NAME = "codex-bot"`, `_is_bot_only_discovery_pr` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Other pipeline writers use `claude-bot` (`scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:340`, `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:323`, `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:3437`), so an autofix or merge-resolve commit makes `bot_only` false.
  WHY: Such a PR is reported as `kept_human_commits` and stays open, so the stale-PR conflict persists on Claude-engine consumers. The outcome name is misleading.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:`SEED_PR_TITLE_PREFIX`, matched against the title at scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:788 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The prefix is a hard-coded copy of a title built in another module, and no test ties the two together.
  WHY: If the title wording changes, `reason=manifest_already_committed` stops firing and the tests still pass.
- HARDENING: `list_open_discovery_prs` gives no signal when the result is exactly `DISCOVERY_PR_LIST_LIMIT`. Suggested fix: if `len(payload) >= DISCOVERY_PR_LIST_LIMIT`, return a non-fatal truncation note or log a diagnostic (~4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:75, 96-104 (list_open_discovery_prs) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR listing is capped at 100 PRs before filtering for discovery branches.
  WHY: Discovery PRs older than the 100th open PR are omitted and never closed by the superseded-PR sweep, so the stale-manifest conflict stays unresolved.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:63, 103-116 (_is_bot_only_discovery_pr) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The bot-only guard ignores commits by `claude-bot` (`scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:340`).
  WHY: Discovery PRs with Claude-engine autofix or merge-resolve commits get `bot_only=False` and are never closed automatically, so stale PRs persist.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:66, 178 (close_superseded_discovery_prs) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `SEED_PR_TITLE_PREFIX` is tightly coupled to the title generation in `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py`, with no shared constant or contract test.
  WHY: If the title logic changes, `reason=manifest_already_committed` silently stops matching and stale seed PRs are not cleaned up.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:154, 218 (close_superseded_discovery_prs) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: There is a TOCTOU race in the human-commit guard.
  WHY: `list_open_discovery_prs` snapshots commit history at the start of the cycle, and a human push before `gh pr close` leaves a PR with human edits that still gets closed.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:975-985 (list_open_discovery_prs); `DISCOVERY_PR_LIST_LIMIT = 100` at line 72; prefix filter at line 1014 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `--limit 100` is applied by `gh pr list` before the branch-prefix filter, so on a consumer with more than 100 open PRs the older discovery PRs are paged out and neither cleanup pass sees them.
  WHY: The superseded seed PR (the btc_sweeper#196 shape) stays open and conflicts, which is the failure this PR exists to prevent.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:`_is_bot_only_discovery_pr` (lines 928-946); consumed at lines 1103 and 1134; scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:882-968, listing at line 659, post-create close at lines 855-868 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `bot_only` is a list-time snapshot and `gh pr close` runs later, which contradicts the promise that a PR with any non-`codex-bot` commit is never closed.
  WHY: A user push or force-push during the gap, which can last minutes in the second pass, still leads to the PR being closed.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:`SEED_PR_TITLE_PREFIX` at line 66, matched at line 1083; the runner title is at scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:787-788 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The constant and the runner's title-generation site are coupled across two files, and the test fixtures (`SEED_TITLE` at tests/test_validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:842, `SWEEP_SEED_TITLE` at tests/test_validation_refresh_runner.py:1670) are hand-built.
  WHY: A runner-side title rewrite silently disables `manifest_already_committed` while every test still passes.
- scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py and scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:1134-1146; gate at scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:891-896 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The runner now issues mutating `gh pr close` calls every cycle by default, and the dataclass default of `True` means a caller that builds a `DiscoveryRunContext` directly inherits the sweep.
  WHY: The gate is documented but easy to miss. Existing tests opt out explicitly (tests/test_validation_refresh_runner.py:654).
- HARDENING 1: Re-check `bot_only` just before close with `gh pr view <num> --json commits`, and downgrade to `kept_human_commits` if any commit is not by `codex-bot`. It belongs in `close_superseded_discovery_prs` between lines 1102 and 1133 (~12 lines, risk 3).
- HARDENING 2: Use `--search "head:automation/validate-discovery/"` or paginate to avoid the >100 miss in `list_open_discovery_prs` around line 983 (~6 lines, risk 3).
- HARDENING 3: Add a contract test in tests/test_validation_refresh_runner.py, after line ~1812, asserting the runner's seed-PR title starts with `SEED_PR_TITLE_PREFIX` (~6 lines, risk 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  PROBLEM: `--limit 100` truncates the open-PR results before the code filters for discovery branches.

- scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:659-664, 855-865; scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:1103-1145 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
